sentences.en: Today's lecture is about studies that look at how music therapy can be used to help patients who undergo surgery. Now, most people undergo a surgical procedure at some point in their lives. And more than fifty-one million operations are performed annually in the USA.
sentences.zh: 今天的讲座主题是探讨音乐治疗如何帮助接受手术的患者。目前，大多数人在一生中都会经历某种外科手术。仅在美国，每年就进行超过五千一百万例手术。

sentences.en: But there's no escaping the fact that most patients feel uncomfortable following surgery.
sentences.zh: 但不可否认的是，大多数患者在术后都会感到不适。

sentences.en: They may have difficulty mobilising, and even sitting up in bed can feel too much. They may also be negatively affected by having their routine disturbed, you know, like if they can't do the things they normally do, or have to devote a lot of time to appointments such as physiotherapy, to aid their recovery.
sentences.zh: 他们可能难以活动，甚至在床上坐起来都感觉十分吃力。此外，日常作息被打乱也会对他们产生负面影响，比如无法照常进行日常活动，或不得不花费大量时间前往物理治疗等复健预约。

sentences.en: Currently. the main strategy for improving recovery is medication to control pain, and this can be administered to patients in the short, medium or longer term, depending on the extent of their surgery. But music is still not an everyday part of the post-surgical phase. despite a wealth of relevant studies supporting its potential in recovery.
sentences.zh: 目前，改善术后康复的主要策略是使用止痛药物，这些药物可根据手术范围的大小，在短期、中期或更长时间内给予患者。然而，尽管已有大量相关研究支持音乐在康复过程中的潜在作用，音乐仍未成为术后常规护理的一部分。

sentences.en: Earlier this year, a research team set out to assess all the available evidence so that they could highlight the potential for music in surgical recovery. They identified nearly a hundred trials involving a total of seven thousand patients who were played recorded music as part of their post-operative care. The researchers then looked at what impact the music had on the patients. They discovered that patients who had been played music reported feeling happier and more satisfied in the post-operative phase, and the length of their stay was shorter than for patients who had not listened to any music.
sentences.zh: 今年早些时候，一支研究团队着手全面评估所有现有证据，以凸显音乐在术后康复中的潜力。他们共识别出近一百项临床试验，涉及总计七千名患者；这些患者在术后护理期间均接受了录音音乐干预。随后，研究人员考察了音乐对患者产生的影响。他们发现，聆听音乐的患者在术后阶段报告心情更愉悦、满意度更高，且住院时间比未听音乐的患者更短。

sentences.en: The researchers also explored the patients' choice of music, and their findings showed that a wide variety of music styles was evident. However, a common factor was that the chosen music had a calming quality. Some of the patients listened to music with headphones, but it was quiet enough not to prevent them from being able to communicate with nurses and other staff. More often though, the mode of delivery was by what are known as music pillows. These broadcast sound that is only audible to the person lying on them. The research involved testing music before, during or after operations or a combination. Some patients listened to the music just once a day, while others had several episodes a day.
sentences.zh: 研究人员还调查了患者对音乐类型的选择，结果表明所选音乐风格极为多样。但一个共同特点是：所选音乐普遍具有舒缓 calming 的特质。部分患者通过耳机听音乐，音量足够轻柔，不会妨碍其与护士及其他医护人员交流。但更常见的播放方式是使用所谓‘音乐枕’——这种枕头仅使躺在上面的人能听到所播放的声音。研究涵盖术前、术中、术后单独或联合播放音乐的情形。有些患者每天只听一次音乐，而另一些人则每天多次聆听。

sentences.en: When asked to report their experience of listening to music, surgical patients said that either they had no feelings of anxiety at any point, or those feelings were only slight.
sentences.zh: 当被要求报告听音乐的体验时，外科患者表示，要么全程毫无焦虑感，要么仅有轻微焦虑感。

sentences.en: Patients who hadn't listened to music, on the other hand, reported higher levels of dissatisfaction. This feedback from all of the patients was then cross-checked against their medical notes. And in every case, those who were given music to listen to didn't need as much medication to ease their pain as those patients who weren't played music. The type of music, patient choice and timing, before, during or after the surgery didn't make much difference. And it even worked when patients were played music under general anaesthetic, although the positive effects were greater when patients were awake.
sentences.zh: 相比之下，未听音乐的患者报告了更高程度的不满。研究人员将所有患者的反馈与其病历记录交叉核对，结果发现：所有听过音乐的患者，所需止痛药剂量均少于未听音乐的患者。音乐类型、患者自主选择以及播放时机（术前、术中或术后）均未产生显著差异；即便在全身麻醉状态下播放音乐也有效果，不过当患者处于清醒状态时，积极效应更为明显。

sentences.en: All the evidence suggests that music has a positive effect on post-operative patients, but it's not entirely clear how or why this is the case. A lot of people listen to music in daily life as a way to relax and forget their problems, but the researchers came to the conclusion that it worked on patients by distraction. I suppose it was something familiar and gave them something they could control.
sentences.zh: 所有证据均表明，音乐对术后患者具有积极影响，但其具体作用机制及原因尚不完全明确。许多人日常生活中听音乐是为了放松并暂时忘却烦恼，但研究人员最终得出结论：音乐主要通过‘分散注意力’的方式起效。我想，这或许是因为音乐令人熟悉，且赋予患者一种可控感。

sentences.en: The researchers say there is now sufficient research to demonstrate that music should be available to all patients undergoing operations. They say patients should be able to choose what they'd like to listen to, and if they prefer, recordings taken from nature can be just as good as music. Surgical teams may prefer patients to listen to music before the procedure or as soon as they arrive back onto the ward. Clearly, there's more to learn about this area, and the team now plan to focus their next research on the most appropriate volume to play the music at. And I look forward to reading the results of their study.
sentences.zh: 研究人员指出，目前已有充分的研究证据表明，音乐理应向所有接受手术的患者开放提供。他们建议患者应能自主选择想听的内容，若患者偏好，来自大自然的录音效果亦可与音乐相当。外科团队可能更倾向于让患者在手术前或刚返回病房时即开始听音乐。显然，该领域仍有诸多待探索之处，研究团队下一步计划聚焦于确定播放音乐的最适宜音量。我期待阅读他们后续研究的结果。

sentences.en: It will be interesting to see...
